{{Top|fa}} {{Otheruses|Kent}} {{Character |type=Galactic Empire |image=[[File:KentDeezling.png]] |name=Kent Deezling |homeworld= |birth= |death=[[1 BBY]], [[Scarif]]''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' establishes that Deezling was [[Death|killed]] on [[Scarif]] during the events of ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', which are dated to [[1 BBY]] by ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''. |species=[[Human]]''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' {{C|French version only}} |gender=[[Gender|Male]]{{HelmetCollectionCite|56|Helmets}} |pronouns=He/him |height= |mass= |hair= |feathers= |eyes= |skin=Light''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' |cyber= |families= |parents= |partners= |siblings= |children= |affiliation=[[Galactic Empire]] |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|Cargo shuttle ''SW-0608'', be prepared to receive inspection team.|Frobb informs the crew of ''SW-0608'' that Deezling and Hakelia are about to board|audio=Frobb.flac|''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''}} '''Kent Deezling''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who worked as a [[Imperial ground crew|deck technician]] in the [[Imperial Center of Military Research]] on the [[planet]] [[Scarif]]. His duties for the [[Galactic Empire]] included directing traffic, checking landing platform equipment, guard duty, and conducting routine inspections on newly arrived [[Starship|vessels]]. In [[1 BBY]], Deezling was assigned to [[Landing Platform Nine]] on Scarif and accompanied [[Lieutenant]] [[Colin Hakelia]] and two [[stormtrooper]]s for an inspection of the [[Zeta-class Heavy Cargo Shuttle|''Zeta''-class Heavy Cargo Shuttle]] ''[[SW-0608]]'' when it landed there. The [[shuttle]] carried a [[Rogue One|group]] of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|rebels]] seeking to [[Battle of Scarif|steal]] the [[Death Star plans|plans]] to the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]], and they captured Deezling and his team once they came aboard. The rebel [[Jyn Erso]] then took Deezling's [[Clothing|uniform]] and used it to infiltrate the [[Citadel Tower]] where the plans were kept. Deezling [[Death|perished]] during the ensuing battle and destruction of the Imperial complex. ==Biography== ===Traffic director=== [[File:DeezlingEntrance-RO.png|thumb|left|300px|Kent Deezling worked on the Imperial landing pads of Scarif.]] Kent Deezling was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who served the [[Galactic Empire]] as a [[Imperial ground crew|deck technician]] in the [[Imperial Center of Military Research]] around the [[Citadel Tower]] on the [[planet]] [[Scarif]]. Although support personnel were generally ignored or sneered at by higher ranking [[Imperial officer]]s, the sterling routine work of individuals like Deezling kept the Imperial war machine going as he played a vital part in the process of coordinating incoming and outgoing flights on Scarif. Plugged into air traffic control via a [[headset]], Deezling worked in concert with flight-control [[technician]]s stationed in the tower, whom he liaised with constantly. At the base, Deezling had a variety of duties, including directing traffic manually on rapidly changing landing fields where automated systems could not react quickly enough and helping [[pilot]]s to maneuver their [[Starship|ships]] using illuminated traffic wands when they were landing or taking off. Deezling was also authorized to commandeer certain vessels and pilot them to their proper positions on a landing deck, with deck technicians receiving the training necessary to control a wide number of craft. Deezling and other technicians also acted as [[inspector]]s, ensuring landing pad equipment was functional and priming accompanying ground crew when conducting routine inspection checks on recently landed vessels as part of a team that also included an Imperial [[officer]] and a [[stormtrooper]] escort.''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' Deezling also acted as a guard.[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' novelization]] ===Routine inspection=== [[File:InspectionTeamBoarding-RO.png|thumb|right|300px|Kent Deezling was part of the team sent to inspect ''SW-0608''.]] In [[1 BBY]], Deezling was posted to [[Landing Platform Nine]] on Scarif, where he and [[Lieutenant]] [[Colin Hakelia]] were part of an inspection team that [[Second Lieutenant]] [[Frobb]], [[deck officer]] of the platform, sent to inspect the [[Zeta-class Heavy Cargo Shuttle|''Zeta''-class Heavy Cargo Shuttle]] ''[[SW-0608]]'' after it arrived there. Escorted by two stormtroopers, Deezling and Hakelia left the tram station that connected the landing platform to the Citadel Tower and approached the [[shuttle]]. The deck technician then pulled a lever on the vessel's exterior that deployed the entry ramp. The inspection team boarded with no idea that the routine operation would end in tragedy for them, as ''SW-0608'' had been [[Mission to Eadu|stolen]] from the Empire by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] and carried a [[Rogue One|group]] of rebels seeking to [[Battle of Scarif|steal]] the [[Death Star plans|plans]] to the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]]. ===Expect the uninspected=== {{Quote|Hello."
"Hey. You're probably looking for a manifest."
"That would be helpful.|Hakelia greets Rook as he and Deezling board the shuttle|}} In the ship's hold, Deezling and his team were greeted by the defected Imperial pilot [[Bodhi Rook]], who directed them below to find the ship's manifest. At the hatch down into the cargo area, the inspection team was met by the rebel [[Baze Malbus]] aiming his [[MWC-35c "Staccato Lightning" repeating cannon|weapon]] at them. When Rook and a number of other rebels also trained their weapons on the Imperials, Deezling and the others surrendered.''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel]]'' From the [[cockpit]], the rebel [[Jyn Erso]] heard a muffled cry and the sound of several impacts against the deck. The Imperials were then tied up and stripped of their uniforms, and the [[prisoner]]s were stowed away in the cargo area of the vessel. [[File:DeezlingDisguise-RO.png|thumb|left|300px|Jyn Erso used Kent Deezling's uniform as a disguise.]] Erso then donned Deezling's [[Clothing|uniform]] as a disguise. Although it was too big for her, she used it to infiltrate the Citadel Tower, where she succeeded in stealing the Death Star plans. Fighting broke out between the rebels and Imperials, with ''SW-0608'' destroyed in an explosion and the entire Imperial compound eventually destroyed by the [[Death Star]]. At some point during these events, Deezling and the rest of the inspection team [[Death|perished]]. ==Personality and traits== Deck technicians such as Deezling generally preferred analog solutions to problems and could eyeball distances without [[sensor]]s. He had light skin. ==Equipment== [[File:DeezlingLever-RO.png|thumb|right|300px|Kent Deezling wore a sealed helmet while working in dusty and windy conditions on Scarif.]] While on Scarif, Deezling wore a [[Color|black]] [[Imperial military uniforms|Imperial flight jumpsuit]] for instances where he needed to pilot a vessel in order to ensure the safe and smooth operation of the landing platform. The suit also included pockets for tools and equipment needed in his [[Standard day|daily]] tasks and a chest-mounted [[flight pack]] that included sensors to aid Deezling in his work. It was worn with black [[glove]]s and black boots that provided additional grip and a black [[utility belt]], on which Deezling carried a spare [[Power cell|power pack]] that could be used for the suit's systems or the pair of illuminated traffic wands that he wore on his back. Deezling's uniform also included a black wraparound [[helmet]] that was fully sealed, equipped with an integrated [[Air-filtration system|air filtration system]], and covered his whole head in order to protect him from the noise and pollution of his dusty and windy work environment and allow him to better concentrate. The helmet's visor provided a constant stream of information to Deezling about his surroundings and allowed him to see through dust and fumes, although in order to let Deezling view some problems with his own eyes, it could be flipped down into the helmet's faceplate, which itself was also removable. The helmet also included a [[comlink]] that let him communicate with air traffic control, pilots, and other landing platform crew. ==Behind the scenes== ===Production=== {{Quote|Toward the end of the film, when they land at the Imperial base, Jyn and Cassian have to put on disguises. We put her in this very cool outfit: an Imperial landing-pad guard. This is how she manages to get through the Imperial base. It's three looks together—a play on the Imperial gunner's helmet but with a moveable visor and underbite.|David Crossman, on Kent Deezling's costume|''[[The Art of Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''}} [[File:DeezlingCostumeConcept-ArtOfRO.png|thumb|right|300px|Concept art of Jyn Erso in Kent Deezling's costume]] Kent Deezling first appeared in the [[Star Wars Anthology Series|Anthology Series]] film, ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', as well as in its [[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|adult]] and [[Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel|junior novelizations]], which released the same day as the film on [[December 16]], [[2016]].{{SW|url=news/rebel-reading-rogue-one-books|text=Rebel Reading: A Guide to ''Rogue One'' Books|author=[[James Floyd|Floyd, James]]|date=2016-12-14}} Prior to the release of the film, the character was first revealed in a featurette for ''Rogue One'' released on [[November 16]], 2016.{{SWYouTube|u5sdztM-p98|Rogue One: A Star Wars Story Featurette|sw_url=video/rogue-one-a-star-wars-story-intro-featurette}} According to co-costume designer [[Dave Crossman|David Crossman]], the character's costume combined three different looks, including the helmet of an [[Imperial weapons technician|Imperial gunner]] modified to show the character's face. At least three pieces of concept art for Deezling's costume were created by co-costume designer [[Glyn Dillon]].''[[The Art of Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' ===Pick up shots=== Actor [[Scott Stevenson]] portrayed Kent Deezling, known during production as "HeroTrooper." Over the course of a day, the visual effects team captured pickup shots, promotional stills photography, and "Sprite" shots in which Stevenson performed actions in front of a blue screen that could be edited into the film.{{EmailCite|email=File:ScottStevensonEmail.png|creator=[[Scott Stevenson]]|date=2023-12-28}} Although none of the pickup shots of Stevenson as Deezling were used in the final film, some "Sprite" shots were used and the promotional stills were used in various other media. This included the reference book ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'', which was written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and released on the same day as the film as the first source to identify Deezling. ==Appearances== {{Indexpage}} {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Kent Deezling}} *''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' {{1st|[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|novelization]], and ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel]]''}} *[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' novelization]] {{Ab|Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (audiobook)}} {{Imo}} *''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel]]'' {{Ab|Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel (audiobook)}} *[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story Graphic Novel Adaptation|''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' Graphic Novel Adaptation]] *[[Rogue One Adaptation 5|''Rogue One Adaptation'' 5]] ==Sources== *{{SWYouTube|u5sdztM-p98|Rogue One: A Star Wars Story Featurette|sw_url=video/rogue-one-a-star-wars-story-intro-featurette}} {{1stp}} *{{SWYouTube|BBNc7Pz35OA|Rogue One: A Star Wars Story "Breath" TV Spot}} {{Video}} *''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' {{1stID|Kent Deezling}} *''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Ultimate Sticker Encyclopedia]]'' *{{HelmetCollectionCite|49|Highlights of the Saga}} {{Imo}} {{SourceContents|issue={{HelmetCollectionCite|56|parent=1}}|contents= *{{HelmetCollectionCite|56|Helmets}} *{{HelmetCollectionCite|56|Highlights of the Saga}} }} *''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A -
